'''''Goeppertia warszewiczii''''' (previously ''Calathea warscewiczii'') is a species of perennial, herbaceous [[plant]] from the genus [[Goeppertia]] in the [[Marantaceae]] family, native to Costa Rica, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Panamá.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Goeppertia warszewiczii (Lem.) Borchs. & S.Suárez {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:77130098-1 |access-date=2026-06-05 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref> The specific epithet ''warszewiczii'' refers to [[Józef Warszewicz]].<ref name="Zemanek">{{cite journal |last1=Zemanek |first1=Alicja |last2=Zemanek |first2=Bogdan |last3=Głuszak |first3=Tomasz |last4=Nobis |first4=Marcin |title=Józef Warszewicz (1812–1866) and taxonomical history of Warszewiczia coccinea (Vahl) Klotzsch |journal=Studia Historiae Scientiarum |date=2021 |volume=20 |pages=601–625 |doi=10.4467/2543702XSHS.21.017.14048 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Description ==
[[File:Goeppertia warszewiczii inflroescence.jpg|left|thumb|170x170px|Inflroescence of ''Goeppertia warszewiczii'']]
''Goeppertia warszeiwczii'' is a medium sized plant with long, dark green velvety [[Leaf|leaves]], with short and thick; puprle [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]] and short; purple [[pulvinus]]. The leaves usually have a pattern on the upper side of the leaf, with a saw tooth, light green band along the middle vein. The [[inflorescence]] of G.warszewiczii is made of multiple [[Bract|bracts]] around a short, purple [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncle]]. The bracts appear white at first and slowly fade into a deep purple color with time, the [[Flower|flowers]] often stay closed throughout the flowering process until a [[pollinator]] come to open it. The flowers are white creamy. <ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lemaire |first=Charles Antoine |date=1854 |title=Maranta (?) warszewiczii |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/92283 |journal=L'Illustration Horticole |volume=1}}</ref>

== Uses ==
The [[Naso people|Teribe]] use ''Goeppertia warscewiczii'' for treating snakebites.<ref name="Gupta">{{cite journal |last1=Gupta |first1=M. P. |last2=Solis |first2=P. N. |last3=Calderón |first3=A. I. |last4=Guinneau-Sinclair |first4=F. |last5=Correa |first5=M. |last6=Galdames |first6=C. |last7=Guerra |first7=C. |title=Medical ethnobotany of the Teribes of Bocas del Toro, Panama |journal=Journal of Ethnopharmacology |date=2005 |volume=96 |issue=3 |pages=389–401 |doi=10.1016/j.jep.2004.08.032 |pmid=15619557 }}</ref>

== Similar species ==
In, Costa Rica, it is often confused with a very similar species ''[[Goeppertia leucostachys]]''. This later plant has an extremely similar inflorescence and dark green velvety leaves. The key to differenciate those two species is the hair being found on the whole plant of ''G.leucostachys''. On this species, the bracts, peduncle, petioles, leaves are all hairy, unlike on ''Goeppertia warszewiczii''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Curtis |first=William |date=1875 |title=Calathea leucostachys |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/436225 |journal=Curtis's Botanical Magazine |pages=6205}}</ref>
